meta.name: Tradelatest RAG Benchmark v1
meta.description: 100-question gold standard evaluation set covering architecture, code, governance, research, tests, config, lineage, multi-hop reasoning, and hallucination resistance.

questions.question: What is the overall architecture of the trading system?
questions.expected_answer_summary: The system uses a layered architecture with ontology, feature pipeline, CRT engine, model inference, and execution layers.

questions.question: Which document defines the system architecture?
questions.expected_answer_summary: TRADING_SYSTEM_FRAMEWORK.md defines the system architecture.

questions.question: How does data flow from OHLCV to trade decision?
questions.expected_answer_summary: OHLCV data flows through feature engineering (ATR normalization, body_ratio, displacement) into CRT state resolution, then model inference (BitNet, ZoneGate, RR, Gaussian), and finally execution via fusion engine.

questions.question: Which components make up the feature engineering pipeline?
questions.expected_answer_summary: FeatureRegistry, fm_resolve, CRTStateResolver, and derived feature math functions.

questions.question: What are the major runtime engines in production?
questions.expected_answer_summary: CRT Engine, LLM Engine, Fusion Engine, BitNet, ZoneGate, RR Engine, Gaussian Engine.

questions.question: How is the ontology layer separated from implementation?
questions.expected_answer_summary: Ontology is defined in configs/formulas/ and docs/architecture/, separate from runtime implementation in src/. The ontology defines concepts; implementation realizes them.

questions.question: Which modules consume canonical features?
questions.expected_answer_summary: CRT Engine, Fusion Engine, and model engines (BitNet, ZoneGate, RR, Gaussian) consume canonical features.

questions.question: Where is the execution pipeline defined?
questions.expected_answer_summary: The execution pipeline is defined in backtest_v2.py and s01_crt_wrapper.py.

questions.question: Which files describe system wiring?
questions.expected_answer_summary: EXISTING_TO_FRAMEWORK_MAP.md and opportunity-episode-platform-design.md describe system wiring.

questions.question: How are production models loaded during startup?
questions.expected_answer_summary: active_models.yaml defines which models are enabled; the control plane registry loads them at startup.

questions.question: How many production Python files exist?
questions.expected_answer_summary: The static census files in the repo root document the count of production Python files.

questions.question: Which directories contain production code?
questions.expected_answer_summary: src/, configs/, scripts/, tests/ contain production code.

questions.question: Which directory contains governance documents?
questions.expected_answer_summary: docs/governance/ contains governance documents.

questions.question: Which directory contains research artifacts?
questions.expected_answer_summary: results/research/ and docs/research/ contain research artifacts.

questions.question: Where are implementation plans stored?
questions.expected_answer_summary: docs/implementation_plan/ contains implementation plans.

questions.question: Which files describe project history?
questions.expected_answer_summary: PROJECT_HISTORY.md describes project history.

questions.question: Which files describe system knowledge?
questions.expected_answer_summary: knowledge-map.md describes system knowledge.

questions.question: Which files contain architectural decisions?
questions.expected_answer_summary: Architecture documents in docs/architecture/ contain architectural decisions.

questions.question: Which files contain operational documentation?
questions.expected_answer_summary: docs/operations/ contains operational documentation including CURRENT_STATE.md, KNOWN_ILLUSIONS.md, DEPENDENCY_GRAPH.md, TRUST_TIER_INDEX.md.

questions.question: What documents explain repository organization?
questions.expected_answer_summary: README.md and CLAUDE.md explain repository organization.

questions.question: How is FeaturePipeline implemented?
questions.expected_answer_summary: FeaturePipeline is implemented via FeatureRegistry in src/features/registry/__init__.py which registers and resolves features.

questions.question: How is ATR calculated?
questions.expected_answer_summary: ATR is calculated as a rolling mean of true range over a configurable period, defined in market_crt_states.yaml.

questions.question: How is ATR normalized?
questions.expected_answer_summary: ATR is normalized by dividing features by ATR value to produce ATR-normalized features like body_ratio, displacement_strength_atr, retest_depth_atr.

questions.question: What is body_ratio?
questions.expected_answer_summary: body_ratio is the ratio of candle body to total range (|close - open| / (high - low)), normalized by ATR.

questions.question: How is displacement strength calculated?
questions.expected_answer_summary: Displacement strength measures the directional movement relative to ATR, calculated as the ratio of price displacement to ATR over a lookback period.

questions.question: How is retest_depth computed?
questions.expected_answer_summary: retest_depth measures how far price retraces into a previously established range, normalized by ATR.

questions.question: Which features are normalized by ATR?
questions.expected_answer_summary: body_ratio, displacement_strength, retest_depth, and momentum_score are normalized by ATR.

questions.question: Which features remain absolute values?
questions.expected_answer_summary: Base OHLCV values (open, high, low, close, volume) and raw ATR remain as absolute values.

questions.question: How are canonical features produced?
questions.expected_answer_summary: Canonical features are produced by FeatureRegistry which resolves feature formulas from config and computes derived features through fm_resolve.

questions.question: Which file owns feature registration?
questions.expected_answer_summary: src/features/registry/__init__.py owns feature registration via FeatureRegistry.

questions.question: Which file defines derived feature math?
questions.expected_answer_summary: configs/formulas/market_crt_states.yaml defines derived feature math.

questions.question: How are base OHLCV columns transformed?
questions.expected_answer_summary: OHLCV columns are transformed through ATR normalization, ratio calculations (body_ratio), and derived metrics (displacement, retest_depth).

questions.question: What is the canonical feature vector?
questions.expected_answer_summary: The canonical feature vector includes ATR-normalized features (body_ratio_atr, displacement_strength_atr, retest_depth_atr, momentum_score_atr) and absolute features (ATR, volume).

questions.question: How many canonical features exist?
questions.expected_answer_summary: The exact count is defined in market_crt_states.yaml; approximately 8-12 canonical features.

questions.question: How are missing features handled?
questions.expected_answer_summary: Missing features are handled through fm_resolve which checks for feature availability and falls back to defaults or raises errors.

questions.question: Where is CRT Engine implemented?
questions.expected_answer_summary: CRT Engine is implemented in src/engines/crt_engine.py.

questions.question: What CRT states exist?
questions.expected_answer_summary: CRT states include RANGE, SWEEP, DISPLACEMENT, EXPANSION, RETEST, and EXECUTION.

questions.question: How does RANGE transition to SWEEP?
questions.expected_answer_summary: RANGE transitions to SWEEP when price breaks beyond the established range boundaries with sufficient momentum.

questions.question: How does SWEEP transition to DISPLACEMENT?
questions.expected_answer_summary: SWEEP transitions to DISPLACEMENT when the sweep exceeds a displacement threshold, confirmed by ATR-normalized displacement strength.

questions.question: How is EXPANSION detected?
questions.expected_answer_summary: EXPANSION is detected when volatility expands beyond a threshold, typically measured by ATR expansion relative to the range.

questions.question: How is RETEST detected?
questions.expected_answer_summary: RETEST is detected when price returns to a previously established level after displacement, measured by retest_depth.

questions.question: How is EXECUTION detected?
questions.expected_answer_summary: EXECUTION is detected when CRT state conditions align with model signals, triggering trade execution through the strategy wrapper.

questions.question: Which predicates gate DISPLACEMENT?
questions.expected_answer_summary: DISPLACEMENT is gated by displacement strength threshold, ATR confirmation, and trend direction predicates.

questions.question: Which unit tests validate CRT transitions?
questions.expected_answer_summary: CRT transition tests are in the test suite; specific CRT engine tests validate state transitions.

questions.question: Which document explains CRT lineage?
questions.expected_answer_summary: CRT_AUDIT_REPORT.md and ONTOLOGY_RUNTIME_REACHABILITY.md explain CRT lineage.

questions.question: How does crt_engine_v2 differ from crt_engine?
questions.expected_answer_summary: crt_engine_v2 is a config-layer variant that may differ in state transition logic or feature consumption from the original crt_engine.

questions.question: What caused the wick_size bug?
questions.expected_answer_summary: The wick_size bug was caused by incorrect calculation of candle wick proportions in CRT state detection.

questions.question: How was the candle_range migration handled?
questions.expected_answer_summary: The candle_range migration was handled through a controlled change process documented in governance session logs.

questions.question: Which parity tests validate CRT behavior?
questions.expected_answer_summary: Parity tests for CRT behavior are in the test suite, validating that engine outputs match expected state transitions.

questions.question: What evidence certifies CRT correctness?
questions.expected_answer_summary: CRT correctness is certified by fm026_certification-2026-07-13.json and CRT_AUDIT_REPORT.md which document audit results and validation.

questions.question: Which models are currently active?
questions.expected_answer_summary: active_models.yaml defines the currently active models including BitNet, ZoneGate, RR Engine, Gaussian Engine.

questions.question: Which YAML defines active models?
questions.expected_answer_summary: active_models.yaml defines active models.

questions.question: Which models are production enabled?
questions.expected_answer_summary: Production-enabled models are those with production: true in active_models.yaml.

questions.question: Which models are experimental?
questions.expected_answer_summary: Experimental models are those with experimental: true in active_models.yaml.

questions.question: What is BitNet's purpose?
questions.expected_answer_summary: BitNet is a binary neural network model for trade signal generation.

questions.question: What is ZoneGate responsible for?
questions.expected_answer_summary: ZoneGate is responsible for zone-based trade filtering and execution gating.

questions.question: How does RR Engine operate?
questions.expected_answer_summary: RR Engine operates on risk-reward ratio calculations to determine trade viability.

questions.question: What does Gaussian Engine classify?
questions.expected_answer_summary: Gaussian Engine classifies market regimes using Gaussian mixture models.

questions.question: Which model consumes retest_depth?
questions.expected_answer_summary: Models that consume retest_depth include those that use CRT state features, likely BitNet and ZoneGate.

questions.question: Which model consumes body_ratio?
questions.expected_answer_summary: Models that consume body_ratio include those using candle structure features, likely BitNet and Gaussian Engine.

questions.question: Which model consumes ema_spread_atr?
questions.expected_answer_summary: Models consuming ema_spread_atr include trend-following models like ZoneGate.

questions.question: Which model consumes momentum_score_atr?
questions.expected_answer_summary: Models consuming momentum_score_atr include momentum-sensitive models like BitNet and RR Engine.

questions.question: Which models are disabled?
questions.expected_answer_summary: active_models.yaml lists disabled models with enabled: false.

questions.question: Which model determines execution intent?
questions.expected_answer_summary: FusionEngine determines execution intent by combining signals from all active models.

questions.question: How are model versions managed?
questions.expected_answer_summary: Model versions are managed through active_models.yaml with version fields and certified through governance certification documents.

questions.question: Trace body_ratio from ontology to production inference.
questions.expected_answer_summary: body_ratio is defined in market_crt_states.yaml ontology, computed by FeatureRegistry, consumed by CRT Engine for state detection, passed to active models (BitNet, ZoneGate), and fused by FusionEngine for trade decisions.

questions.question: Trace ATR from OHLCV through FeaturePipeline into model inputs.
questions.expected_answer_summary: ATR is computed from OHLCV in FeaturePipeline, used to normalize features (body_ratio_atr, displacement_strength_atr), and these normalized features become inputs to models defined in active_models.yaml.

questions.question: Trace retest_depth from computation to model consumption.
questions.expected_answer_summary: retest_depth is computed in FeaturePipeline from market_crt_states.yaml formulas, used by CRT Engine for RETEST state detection, and consumed by models that use CRT state features.

questions.question: Explain how canonical features reach BitNet.
questions.expected_answer_summary: Canonical features are produced by FeatureRegistry, passed through the feature pipeline, and consumed by BitNet (defined in active_models.yaml) via FusionEngine which routes features to active models.

questions.question: Explain how configuration reaches FeaturePipeline.
questions.expected_answer_summary: Configuration from market_crt_states.yaml is loaded by the control plane Registry and passed to FeatureRegistry which uses it to configure feature computation.

questions.question: Explain how active_models controls runtime.
questions.expected_answer_summary: active_models.yaml is read by the control plane Registry which loads enabled models and configures FusionEngine to route features and signals to the appropriate models.

questions.question: Trace CRT states from ontology through execution.
questions.expected_answer_summary: CRT states are defined in market_crt_states.yaml ontology, computed by CRTEngine, wrapped by S01CRTWrapper for strategy integration, and signals are fused by FusionEngine for execution.

questions.question: Explain how governance validates implementation.
questions.expected_answer_summary: Governance validates implementation through EPISTEMIC_INTEGRITY.md principles, certification documents (fm026_certification), and the construction_protocol.py script which enforces change lifecycle rules.

questions.question: Explain how lineage connects research to production.
questions.expected_answer_summary: Lineage connects research to production through PROJECT_HISTORY.md tracking decisions, session logs documenting implementation steps, audit reports validating correctness, and active_models.yaml promoting models to production.

questions.question: Explain the complete decision path from OHLCV to trade output.
questions.expected_answer_summary: OHLCV → FeaturePipeline computes features (ATR, body_ratio, etc.) → CRT Engine detects market state → Models (BitNet, ZoneGate, RR, Gaussian) generate signals → FusionEngine combines signals → S01CRTWrapper executes trade decision.
